questions.q: What does the Sentinel investigation graph show?
options: A list of every analytics rule currently enabled in the workspace
A chronological log of every KQL query an analyst has run
A visual map centered on the incident, with lines to every entity involved and how they connect
The billing cost of the incident's underlying data ingestion
questions.explain: The graph puts the incident at the center with lines radiating out to its entities — users, hosts, IPs, and files.

questions.q: What Chapter 3 configuration is the investigation graph directly built from?
options: The workbook's visualization settings
The data connector's ingestion schedule
Entity mapping on the analytics rule
The Log Analytics workspace's retention period
questions.explain: Entity mapping tells Sentinel which raw log fields correspond to a user, host, or IP, which is exactly what the graph needs to draw connections between them.

questions.q: What does an entity timeline show that the investigation graph does not?
options: The names of every analyst who has ever worked that incident
The severity level of every incident in the queue
A list of all data connectors configured in the workspace
That specific entity's full activity history, including things from before the current incident started
questions.explain: The timeline is scoped to one entity across all time, while the graph is scoped to the current incident's entities and connections.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what does the graph reveal about a compromised account?
options: That the account belongs to a specific Azure subscription
That the account's password was changed three times
That the account has no entity mapping configured at all
That the account touched two hosts, one of which talked to an external IP
questions.explain: Following the graph's lines from the user entity to two host entities, and one host on to an external IP, surfaces a lateral-movement pattern at a glance.

questions.q: Why does a thorough investigation use both the graph and an entity timeline together?
options: The timeline replaces the graph entirely once an incident is closed
Sentinel requires both to be opened before an incident can be assigned

The graph gives breadth across the incident's connected entities, while the timeline gives depth into one entity's full history, which together answer whether the incident's real scope reaches further than its alerts
The graph only works for High-severity incidents
questions.explain: Breadth from the graph plus depth from the timeline is how an analyst decides whether an incident is contained to its alerts or reaches further.
